title: Visonaut · Less to maintain
summary: A complete source audit with all 45 choices recorded and no open policy decisions. The local handoff draft maps superseded issue rules, coordinated migrations, and required evidence. It is prepared for review and implementation planning. Issue #1 remains the implementation contract until the authorized repository-contract handoff.
goals: Remove code and infrastructure that no longer serve an active need.
Improve review speed and image focus using Ariakit UI components.
Make capture and deployment easier to operate.
Keep each claim tied to source, a measurement, or a stated limit.
useCases: Capture Ariakit variants from prepared Playwright pages.
Submit a complete trusted run and compare its stored images.
Inspect, approve, reject, and correct visual changes.
Recover failed work and keep private review data private.
nonGoals: No production deployment, data deletion, or credential change in this audit.
No automatic change to the current product contract.
No new framework, service, or abstraction without a clear reduction in work.
No claim of production speed, cost, or capacity from a local prototype.
constraints: Source: Visonaut main at 7e23173, fetched on 29 September 2026. The audit includes the new backup retirement in pull request #154.
GitHub issue #1 still contains the earlier implementation contract. This local revision records the maintainer’s newer design choices; an issue update needs separate authorization.
All 61 revision 9 choices are preserved as history. Later issue changes override parts of that history, including the project name, launch scope, capture workflow, and comparison policy.
The current source has one D1 database per environment. The web app and image comparison service share it. Environment isolation is a separate decision from table count.
The current source already uses copied Ariakit UI components. The UI decision is how to finish that composition and remove duplicate styling.

Service metadata, quarantine bytes, and review data stay private. A07 now selects ordinary one-day CI artifacts for successful capture images, manifests, and environment profiles. A signed Submit job still validates and uploads them. Exact comparison identity, complete trusted captures, and failure-safe checks remain constraints unless an explicit option reopens them.
Local measurements use synthetic data and desktop Chrome. Cloudflare login had expired, so this audit does not certify the live resource inventory, current bills, or deployed limits.
Each example is a proposed model. Changing its controls does not answer its decision. Only an explicit decision selection counts as answered.
The current review support contract is Chrome Desktop and keyboard use. Narrow-screen checks in this artifact also cover desktop zoom; they do not certify mobile review support.

Obsolete product paths do not need deprecation windows: Visonaut is under development and Ariakit is its only supported consumer. Convert Ariakit, then remove old paths in the same change. Preserve data and release integrity where needed.

decisions.recommendation: Native D1 recovery and manual evidence export. State the limited R2 recovery coverage and retire legacy restore code after any needed old-set export.
decisions.invalidates: If losing any currently retained visual evidence after database recovery is unacceptable, native D1 recovery alone is not sufficient; choose combined recovery. A legal or contractual independent-backup requirement also invalidates the recommendation.
decisions.migration: Inspect retained legacy sets and restore needs without exposing secret values. Export or convert any set still needed, rehearse Time Travel against isolated data, and remove the obsolete restore source and fields in one cutover. Preserve applied numbered migrations as history. Do not delete retained objects merely because the old binding was removed.
decisions.risks: Deleting a configured binding is not proof buckets or tokens were removed. Current docs about a backup export credential in .github/workflows/README.md:32 are stale. Do not delete legacy sets or pins based on static inspection.

decisions.recommendation: Point the baseline at an immutable source run. Keep source originals while the baseline or a review uses them. Remove protected copying and separate snapshot byte collection for new baselines. Prefer a whole-run owner pin first, because it uses the current retention model.
decisions.invalidates: If whole-run pins retain much more data than baseline copies, or inherited ownership keeps long chains live, keep copies. Measure retained bytes on real runs before committing to source pins. No automatic global deduplication is justified yet.
decisions.migration: Verify immutable source originals and add the baseline owner pin before switching pointers. Convert still-required copied snapshots to source references, verify them, then remove the copied-snapshot reader. Keep existing bytes until references are accounted for; no permanent dual reader. This does not retain promoted rollback under C01.
decisions.risks: This changes a prior D16 design choice (docs/design-r9.json near line 401) and needs explicit maintainer selection. Pointer baselines still need verification of original bytes and deletion protection. Coordinate protected-image lifetime with C01. A pointer alone must not allow cleanup to remove current accepted images.

decisions.question: Who should wait for visual approval?
decisions.summary: Ariakit Gate implements a second client for Visonaut status. It finds the Submit job, reconstructs its actual attempt from timestamps, repeatedly selects the latest check, waits up to 65 × 12 seconds, and asks the maintainer to rerun Gate if review takes longer. That is 13 minutes of configured polling before API overhead, not a measured run duration. Review completion already belongs to the Visonaut check. The current Gate runs its Visonaut verification only when the app workflow succeeds. A direct, unconditional App check changes this path-selected behavior. It must not leave docs-only changes waiting for a visual run that will never start.

decisions.question: Where should a maintainer find the current decisions after a policy changes?
decisions.summary: The repo has a canonical issue, a 61-decision design archive, deployment instructions, operations instructions, and a current-readiness page. They contain different ages of policy. The historical data is useful, but current entry pages still direct readers to statements that have been superseded.
current: README.md:7 says issue 1 defines requirements. README.md:72-74 links revision 9 and says its design archive records selected behavior.

docs/design-r9.json:9 still describes the private ariakit/ariviso repository. :1614 says no repository, package, domain, or namespace has been created. The current issue snapshot and .github/workflows/README.md:58 say the repository is public and Visonaut is released.

docs/design-r9.json:1461-1485 retains D55 daily combined backup. The current issue 1 body also still contains that requirement and its D55 ledger entry. apps/web/src/operations/README.md:24 and :40 say scheduled SQL-plus-R2 backups are retired and only legacy offline code remains.

.github/workflows/README.md:48 calls CLI 0.3.2 and adapter 0.3.1 the versions pinned by Ariakit. The checked-out package manifests are CLI 0.3.6 and adapter 0.3.2. The manifests alone do not prove Ariakit's installed versions; this statement should be linked to a dated verified receipt rather than presented as current without a date.

The repo intentionally preserves old evidence, and an old measurement is not invalid because it is old. This finding concerns present-tense entry points and decision authority. Do not treat documentation conflicts as permission to restore retired infrastructure or reopen all settled choices.

priorDecisions.question: Where should Ariviso live?
priorDecisions.answer: Separate Ariviso monorepo
priorDecisions.context: Settled: a separate private repository, ariakit/ariviso. D60 changes the earlier working name Visuaria to Ariviso; the original note is retained as history. Ariakit is its first client. Public npm packages do not make the application repository public.

priorDecisions.question: What does A or X change?
priorDecisions.answer: Current variant; separate whole-item actions
priorDecisions.notes: We should also have an option besides side by side and pixel diff that we activate with F and show the full new screenshot only (no old). By the way, what would be the shortcuts for the separate whole-item actions? Maybe Shift+A and Shift+X or Mod+A/Mod+X (Mod=Ctrl or Cmd)?
priorDecisions.context: Settled: A/X changes the current variant. F shows only the new screenshot. Shift+A/X changes the whole item (D21).

priorDecisions.question: What should happen after approval or rejection?
priorDecisions.answer: Go to the next pending variant
priorDecisions.context: Settled: after the server saves a verdict, move to the next pending variant. Proposed detail: wrap once through the visible review order; stay on the current variant when no pending variants remain.

priorDecisions.question: Which variant should open when up/down changes the item?
priorDecisions.answer: Remember the last variant for each item
priorDecisions.context: Settled: remember the last selected variant separately for each item. First visit starts at its first variant. Auto-advance selects the next pending variant and updates that item’s memory.

priorDecisions.question: Should React and Solid share one item?
priorDecisions.answer: Framework is a variant dimension
priorDecisions.context: The current capture names include the framework. Grouping frameworks reduces rows but increases variants per item.

priorDecisions.question: How should the first adapter assign stable item keys?
priorDecisions.answer: Explicit stable keys; fresh first batch
priorDecisions.notes:
We don't need a migration. It's fine if all screenshots are new in the first batch.
Confirmed: explicit keys, fresh first batch, no legacy import.
priorDecisions.context: Confirmed in follow-up: explicit stable keys, a fresh first batch, and no legacy import. All first-batch captures are new. Future key-renaming tools are separate work.

priorDecisions.question: What makes a main-branch run the accepted baseline?
priorDecisions.answer: Full post-merge capture with valid review coverage
priorDecisions.notes: I'm not sure if this is what this option says, but the way I think about it is that when a PR diff is fully approved, once the PR is merged into main, that becomes the baseline. For commits that are made on main directly, if there are diffs, they should fail in CI and wait for approval in visuaria just as if it were a PR. Once the items are approved in visuaria for direct main commits, they are baseline. I also think we should consider that items approved from a PR right before it's merged might drift when they land on main (for example, due to a stale merged branch). In that case, those items that diff on main should be explicitly approved to become the baseline. Anyway, I think my explanation here became more complex than it should be. There should be a simple generic rule for this.
priorDecisions.context: A complete main capture becomes the baseline when every change has valid acceptance. Eligible new items, new variants, and confirmed removals are accepted automatically. Existing-image changes and ineligible restoration or drift need review. Earlier acceptance counts only for exact eligible comparisons.

priorDecisions.question: Can approval carry across retries, rebases, or merge queues?
priorDecisions.answer: Reuse only exact eligible comparison tuples
priorDecisions.context: Candidate image equality alone is insufficient. The reference, profile, comparison policy, and item/variant must also match.

priorDecisions.question: Whose approval is enough to pass?
priorDecisions.answer: One maintainer, including the PR author
priorDecisions.context: When explicit human approval is needed, one current maintainer is enough, including the PR author. Automatic acceptance records its policy as the source, not a fictional reviewer.

priorDecisions.question: When should external fork pull requests get Ariviso runs?
priorDecisions.answer: Maintainer branches first
priorDecisions.notes: The repo has PRs restricted to collaborators only anyway.
priorDecisions.context: Settled: maintainer branches first. The maintainer confirmed that Ariakit currently restricts PRs to collaborators. Fork capture and import are deferred.

priorDecisions.question: Must old runs be recomparable without a new CI job?
priorDecisions.answer: Independent service comparison at launch
priorDecisions.context: Settled: the service compares stored captures independently of CI. Cloudflare Queues plus a separate comparison Worker is the proposed runtime; codec and resource probes remain required.

priorDecisions.question: Can maintainers review before all captures arrive?
priorDecisions.answer: Only after the run is sealed
priorDecisions.context: Early review needs provisional states and exact group scopes. Sealing first avoids new variants arriving after a whole-item action.

priorDecisions.question: Who can view screenshots and review results?
priorDecisions.answer: Private app and review data; public image URLs
priorDecisions.context: The app, review results, reviewer names, and per-image verdicts stay private to current Ariakit maintainers. The maintainer explicitly allows public URLs for validated screenshot bytes. A copied image URL can be read without login.

priorDecisions.question: How does Ariviso determine who is a maintainer?
priorDecisions.answer: Repository write permission or higher
priorDecisions.context: GitHub login does not imply repository permission. Organization membership alone is too broad.

priorDecisions.question: How long should closed-run images remain available?
priorDecisions.answer: 30 days
priorDecisions.context: Always keep active baselines, open reviews, and explicitly pinned evidence. These windows apply to unpinned closed runs.

priorDecisions.question: Should launch storage deduplicate exact bytes across runs?
priorDecisions.answer: Per-run objects first
priorDecisions.context: R2 is cheap at the measured scale. Deduplication lowers repeat writes, but safe deletion needs a shared-blob reference protocol.

priorDecisions.question: Which default visual direction fits review work?
priorDecisions.answer: Compact, mostly flat controls
priorDecisions.context: The prototype uses calm dark surfaces, a compact item list, and words plus color for state. Both options use copied Ariakit UI components.

priorDecisions.question: Which parts need published packages at launch?
priorDecisions.answer: Publish the Playwright adapter and CLI
priorDecisions.context: Settled: publish the Playwright adapter and CLI from the private monorepo. Keep web/server code private. Package names and the supported-version matrix still need a release specification.

priorDecisions.question: Which branches must the first release support?
priorDecisions.answer: Main plus PR and merge-queue runs targeting main
priorDecisions.context: One baseline branch is easier to operate. Release branches require independent baseline selection and promotion.

priorDecisions.question: When should Ariviso block merges?
priorDecisions.answer: Required immediately after setup
priorDecisions.notes:
I still don't understand this. New items should be pre-approved. Isn't that the standard in the industry?
Confirmed: Require Visuaria immediately; automatically approve new items.
priorDecisions.context: Require Ariviso immediately after setup and readiness checks, with no optional pilot. Eligible new items, new variants, and confirmed removals can pass automatically. Unapproved existing changes, rejection, incomplete capture, and stale acceptance still block the required check.

priorDecisions.question: Which shortcuts should change the whole item?
priorDecisions.answer: Shift+A / Shift+X
priorDecisions.context: Settled: Shift+A and Shift+X change the whole item. A/X changes the current variant. Keep Cmd/Ctrl+A for Select All and Cmd/Ctrl+X for Cut.

priorDecisions.question: What should undo do after approval made main the baseline?
priorDecisions.answer: Undo the promotion if it is still current
priorDecisions.context: Settled: undo a saved approval and its promotion atomically if that promoted snapshot is still current. Refuse ordinary undo after a later promotion. Automatic acceptance does not invent a maintainer command in the session undo stack.

priorDecisions.question: Should a new variant of an existing item be approved automatically?
priorDecisions.answer: Automatically approve new variants too
priorDecisions.context: Settled: automatically approve a new variant of an existing item, including a newly added browser, theme, or framework. Apply the same validation and exact acceptance rules as for new items. Changes to a previously accepted variant still need review.

priorDecisions.question: How should rejection work after automatic acceptance promoted main?
priorDecisions.answer: Keep the baseline; correct it in a new main capture
priorDecisions.context: Keep an automatically promoted baseline, including a confirmed removal under D59. Historical X makes no change and the automatic service action creates no Undo command. Correct it through a new complete main capture. Existing-image corrections need review; a restored identity follows D35 exact eligible reuse. D22 still governs saved human approval.

priorDecisions.question: What may Ariviso show in Ariakit’s public GitHub checks?
priorDecisions.answer: Generic status plus a sign-in review link
priorDecisions.context: Generic public GitHub status and a sign-in review link remain selected. Reviewer names and per-image results stay private. D13 now permits direct public image URLs, but does not add images to GitHub check output.

priorDecisions.question: Can A/X edit a human-approved run after it promoted main?
priorDecisions.answer: Allow X to reject and roll back the current promotion
priorDecisions.context: Settled: any current maintainer can reject a human-approved variant and roll back its promotion while that promotion is still current, even after reload or without the original approval command. D22 Undo and D24 automatic-history protection remain separate.

priorDecisions.question: Who prepares each variant in the public capture API?
priorDecisions.answer: Ariakit prepares it; capture one variant per call
priorDecisions.context: Settled: Ariakit prepares the page and calls the public adapter once per variant. The adapter captures that prepared condition; the reporter groups calls by stable item key. Theme, viewport, and page preparation remain in the Ariakit wrapper.

priorDecisions.question: When the next-pending search reaches the end, should it wrap?
priorDecisions.answer: Wrap once to the first pending variant
priorDecisions.context: D03 already selects the next pending variant. This chooses what happens when earlier visible variants still need review. If none remain, stay and announce completion under either option.

priorDecisions.question: Where should removed items appear in the review list?
priorDecisions.answer: Candidate order, then removed items
priorDecisions.context: The list must include candidate and reference-only identities. Existing thumbnail rules stay fixed: a retained item uses its first candidate variant; a wholly removed item uses its first reference variant.

priorDecisions.question: What should D show for a new or removed image?
priorDecisions.answer: Make pixel diff unavailable for this case
priorDecisions.context: F shows the new image, or “Removed — no new image”. S shows the existing image next to a labeled empty pane. D has no ordinary before/after pair in these cases.

priorDecisions.question: Should my Undo history survive a page reload?
priorDecisions.answer: Current review session only
priorDecisions.context: D22/D26 revision checks and D24 automatic-history protection apply in both options. This chooses the lifetime of the personal command stack, not whether audit history survives.

priorDecisions.question: How should one prepared capture be called from a Playwright test?
priorDecisions.answer: A page function with explicit variant metadata
priorDecisions.context: D27 keeps page preparation in Ariakit and one variant per capture call. The exact import, function shape, and metadata boundary are still proposed. Both options require explicit stable item and variant keys.

priorDecisions.question: How should capture clients and the service evolve together?
priorDecisions.answer: Versioned manifest with compatible optional additions
priorDecisions.context: Both paths validate manifests, reject duplicate keys, preserve explicit identities and deterministic ordering, and reject an unknown schema. The choice is the compatibility promise for public clients.

priorDecisions.question: Where is first automatic acceptance reserved for an unused key?
priorDecisions.answer: Per verified PR/main lineage
priorDecisions.context: First automatic acceptance is scoped to a verified PR/main lineage. D07/D08 require exact eligible reuse and review of later drift. Independent PRs do not share introduction records; atomic creation on the active valid attempt remains required.

priorDecisions.question: Should a removed identity need fresh approval when it returns?
priorDecisions.answer: Allow exact eligible earlier acceptance
priorDecisions.notes: Should we automatically accept deleted items too? How's the industry standard?
priorDecisions.context: The selected rule permits an earlier acceptance only when its full comparison tuple, profiles, policy, source revision, and verified lineage remain eligible under D08. A restored key alone is not new. Missing expected reference bytes remain an error. D59 separately accepts confirmed removals automatically. A correction that restores a removed identity follows this D35 rule.

priorDecisions.question: May a later full main run pass an earlier pending run?
priorDecisions.answer: Yes, after a complete comparison
priorDecisions.context: Both options preserve full snapshots, ancestry checks, exact acceptance, and refusal of stale promotions. This chooses scheduling when main receives another commit before review finishes.

priorDecisions.question: Should launch accept intentionally partial capture runs?
priorDecisions.answer: Accept full runs only at launch
priorDecisions.context: Only a full trusted run can infer removals, promote main, or satisfy the required check. This chooses whether informational subset runs exist at launch.

priorDecisions.question: How should failed-job-only workflow reruns work?
priorDecisions.answer: Inherit verified successful shards
priorDecisions.context: GitHub test retries and workflow reruns are different. A new workflow attempt must have complete trusted coverage before it can pass; incompatible shards cannot be combined.

priorDecisions.question: Where should the authoritative capture plan live?
priorDecisions.answer: Ariakit’s trusted main configuration
priorDecisions.context: The plan defines the full suite invocation and required jobs. A PR manifest cannot prove its own completeness or relax its gate. Changes to trusted plan configuration need a deliberate rollout in both options.

priorDecisions.question: Which private capture upload path should launch use?
priorDecisions.answer: GitHub OIDC and short-lived capabilities
priorDecisions.context: Uploads enter private quarantine. D13 permits validated image URLs to be public; manifests, diagnostics, and review data stay private. Upload capabilities cannot read private data, approve, or promote. Bind ingest to verified repository, workflow, run, attempt, and tested commit.

priorDecisions.question: How should image bytes reach private quarantine?
priorDecisions.answer: Bounded upload through the Worker
priorDecisions.context: This applies to direct uploads after authorization. Encrypted artifact transport uses the import path instead. Both options hash and validate bytes on the trusted side before they become eligible.

priorDecisions.question: Which image and color contract should launch accept?
priorDecisions.answer: Lossless WebP and PNG
priorDecisions.notes: I don't understand this question. Aren't we using webp?
priorDecisions.context: Ariakit already captures lossless WebP through Playwright 1.63. The follow-up selects both lossless WebP and PNG originals. Preserve their bytes and test both decoders against a defined sRGB and alpha contract; unknown profiles fail clearly. No legacy import is needed.

priorDecisions.question: Which pixel-difference policy should launch use?
priorDecisions.answer: Select a new policy from a defect/noise study
priorDecisions.context: The existing helper uses threshold 0 and maxDiffPixelRatio 0.0005; full-page tolerance is zero. Effective policy comes from trusted configuration, and changes invalidate incompatible acceptance.

priorDecisions.question: How should the adapter confirm stable pixels?
priorDecisions.answer: Adapter preserves current assertion stability
priorDecisions.context: D27 keeps theme and page preparation in Ariakit. Stability is a separate bounded capture check. A timeout fails the capture, including new items; stable dimensions alone cannot pass.

priorDecisions.question: What if the comparison Worker fails codec or resource tests?
priorDecisions.answer: Worker first; test a Container fallback
priorDecisions.context: D11 already requires independent service comparison. Keep originals, deterministic results, bounded retries, and the queue contract under every runtime option. No runtime probe has passed yet.

priorDecisions.question: How long may image-read permission be cached?
priorDecisions.answer: Up to five minutes for reads
priorDecisions.notes: If I understand correctly, we will be limiting image read directly on R2? Is it complex? I mean, I just wanted the app to stay private to maintainers, but I don't mind if the images can be directly accessed. Is this an issue?
priorDecisions.context: Recorded selection: up to five minutes for protected image reads. The later public-image clarification makes this policy inactive for launch image delivery. Public images have no image-read permission check. This answer does not create a five-minute cache policy for private app metadata; protected app routes retain current permission checks.

priorDecisions.question: Which image storage and delivery path should launch use?
priorDecisions.answer: Private R2 Standard with public Worker image URLs
priorDecisions.context: The maintainer retained private R2 Standard storage and clarified that image URLs may be public. Keep exact per-run originals and 30-day unpinned closed-run retention. The app and review data remain private.

priorDecisions.question: What if Better Auth with D1 fails deployed validation?
priorDecisions.answer: Keep D1 and block launch until a supported setup passes
priorDecisions.context: The requested GitHub-only Better Auth stack stays fixed. Current evidence is documentation and issue research, not a working deployment. This choice defines the failure response.

priorDecisions.question: What names should the public adapter and CLI use?
priorDecisions.answer: ariviso CLI and @ariviso/playwright adapter
priorDecisions.notes: We should also register "visuaria" just in case. But I also want to discuss the name. Is visuaria a good name? Can you suggest better alternatives? It's important that good domain TLDs, npm package names, and npm namespaces are available. For example, I thought about visionaria, which has the visionaria.dev domain available (does "vision" + "aria" make sense for a visual regression tool like this?). But it would be awesome if we could come up with a name that has a .com available. I don't know. Suggest a bunch of options after checking their availability.
priorDecisions.context: D60 and the D61 follow-up replace the original naming targets: ariviso is the only CLI package, and @ariviso/playwright is the adapter. The selected repository is ariakit/ariviso. Historical naming options and the original note remain below. Registry control must still be proved before release.

priorDecisions.question: Which toolchain must the first public release support?
priorDecisions.answer: Ariakit’s pinned toolchain first
priorDecisions.context: D18 leaves the supported-version matrix open. Choose the scope, then record exact tested versions before publication. Capture browsers are distinct from the browsers used to review images.

priorDecisions.question: Which operations should the public CLI expose at launch?
priorDecisions.answer: Upload, finalize, and status only
priorDecisions.context: In both options, a successful upload means complete data was accepted, not that visual review passed. Capture/upload errors return nonzero; status supports text and JSON. Capture CI does not wait for human approval. Exact flags and exit-code tables must follow the selected scope.

priorDecisions.question: What evidence must pass before the required check launches?
priorDecisions.answer: Complete the full readiness set
priorDecisions.context: D20 remains required immediately after setup, with no optional pilot. This question defines setup evidence. Both choices require the client combinations selected in D50, review paths selected in D53, and limits required by D54 to pass. Staging covers only expansion beyond those contracts. Selecting a plan does not mark any production test passed or authorize implementation.

priorDecisions.question: Which review-browser and accessibility paths must pass at launch?
priorDecisions.answer: Chrome Desktop and keyboard-only review
priorDecisions.notes: This will be used internally at first so we only need Chrome Desktop for now and keyboard-only use.
priorDecisions.context: Selected launch review support: Chrome Desktop and keyboard-only operation. Verify shortcuts and exclusions, focus, readable states, and zoom. Other review browsers, mobile workflows, and screen-reader certification are deferred. The screenshot capture browser matrix is unchanged.

priorDecisions.question: How should performance and cost limits be chosen?
priorDecisions.answer: Measure first, then approve numeric limits
priorDecisions.notes: My account already has Workers Paid, and I think I'm already using R2 for another project. Also, keep in mind that the number of snapshots in the repo will increase a lot, probably 10x more what we have today, but the sizes might also decrease since right now we have a bunch of ariakit-ui sandbox snapshots that consist of several examples in single images. I did this to reduce the image bloat in the repo and reviews, but the idea with Visuaria is to separate them (plus we will have more examples and sandboxes).
priorDecisions.context: The account already has Workers Paid and may have other R2 use. Plan about ten times the current image count, with a lower but unmeasured mean size after splitting composite captures. Measure bytes, object operations, CPU, review latency, pins, backups, and shared-account incremental cost. Numeric limits remain a later decision.

priorDecisions.question: What recovery plan should launch provide?
priorDecisions.answer: Daily combined backup and tested manual restore
priorDecisions.context: Back up database records and all original images needed for accepted baselines and retained reviews. Test both together. Apply current access and expiry rules after restore. D15 normal-run retention stays unchanged; backup copies have their own stated lifetime.

priorDecisions.question: How should stalled service work reach a maintainer?
priorDecisions.answer: Automatic recovery, then an actionable alert
priorDecisions.context: Bounded retries, reconciliation, visible failure, and safe manual recovery are required in both options. A service outage never reports success. Select numeric deadlines from validated workloads. This design does not send or authorize messages.

priorDecisions.question: Where should end-to-end GitHub behavior be proved before cutover?
priorDecisions.answer: Disposable repository, then separate Ariakit diagnostics
priorDecisions.context: D20 rejects an optional production pilot. These are pre-launch tests while Ariakit’s existing required visual workflow remains in place. Separate authorization is still needed to create repositories, deploy, or write checks.

priorDecisions.question: Can a recovered Playwright retry produce an eligible capture?
priorDecisions.answer: Use the final successful test attempt
priorDecisions.context: This is a retry of one test inside a workflow attempt, not D38’s job rerun. Exhausted retries and missing required captures fail in both options. Earlier failed-attempt images remain private diagnostics.

priorDecisions.question: Should confirmed removals be accepted automatically?
priorDecisions.answer: Automatically accept confirmed removals
priorDecisions.context: A complete trusted run automatically accepts a confirmed item or variant removal. Missing, failed, corrupt, or unavailable required captures remain errors. Keep a visible removal row, exact acceptance history, and the existing rejection and reuse guards. D24 protects automatically promoted removals; D35 controls a later restoration.

priorDecisions.question: Which project name should replace the current naming targets, if any?
priorDecisions.answer: Ariviso
priorDecisions.context: Selected name: Ariviso. The private repository target is ariakit/ariviso. D61’s explicit follow-up selects ariviso as the only CLI package and @ariviso/playwright as the adapter. No domain, repository, package, or namespace has been created. Registry evidence remains provisional.

priorDecisions.question: What should the bare project-name package provide?
priorDecisions.answer: ariviso as the only CLI package
priorDecisions.notes: Let's do ariviso for the CLI (and use @ariviso/\* for other packages like playwright).
priorDecisions.context: Confirmed in follow-up: ariviso is the only CLI package. Use @ariviso/* for other packages, starting with @ariviso/playwright. Do not publish @ariviso/cli. This is a functional package choice, not an empty name reservation; publication is outside this design task.
